shared_context.content: For integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, K_{m,g} is the set of tuples k=(k_1,...,k_{m-1}) of positive integers such that k_1+...+k_{m-1}=g and, for all integers i,j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1: if i+j < m then k_i+k_j >= k_{i+j}, and if i+j > m then k_i+k_j+1 >= k_{i+j-m}.
shared_context.label: K_m_g_definition

shared_context.content: A numerical semigroup is a subset S of N={0,1,2,...} containing 0, closed under addition, and with finite complement. Its multiplicity is the smallest positive element of S. Its genus is the number of elements of N not in S. If S has multiplicity m, then for each residue r in {1,...,m-1}, the Apery element w_r is the least element of S congruent to r modulo m, and the associated Kunz coordinate is k_r=(w_r-r)/m.
shared_context.label: numerical_semigroup_and_apery

strategy_summary: Translate the tuple sets K_{m,g} into numerical semigroups of multiplicity m via Kunz coordinates, prove this translation is a bijection at genus g and at genus g+1, invoke a monotonicity theorem for the cardinalities of fixed-multiplicity numerical semigroups, convert that finite cardinality inequality into an injection on the semigroup side, and transport the injection back to tuples.
